observations: A large black rounded mass occupies the upper-left quadrant, with a red cross-mark near its top and yellow diagonal lines radiating from its left edge toward the upper corner.
A red-orange disc sits right of center, filled with concentric white spiral rings; orange and yellow jagged marks cluster around and beneath it.
Across the white background, small black marks—dashes, hooks, and short strokes—scatter broadly, while looping lines in blue, pink, yellow, and white weave through the mid-ground.
reading: Two heavy forms—one black, one red—press close near center, the spiral on the red disc pulling the eye inward while the black mass holds with flat opacity. Scattered marks across the white field read as restless noise around a tense core. Yellow lines cut sharp angles against the rounded forms, and the overall feeling is one of pressure held just short of release.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #155 and nnxyz nnotb #157 share a loose scattered-mark field, but #156 replaces their bright open backgrounds with a white ground that makes the black mass feel heavier and more isolated.

connections.reason: Both works place a tightly wound spiral inside a circular form against a dark surrounding mass—here a red disc with white rings, there an orange-red circle with a white cross—making the spiral the focal anchor in each.

nnxyz nnotb #155 uses the same scattered small-mark field across a light ground, but its yellow spiral forms sit inside a grey rounded shape rather than beside a separate black mass, offering a direct structural contrast.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first—on the concentric rings of the red disc, the flat black mass beside it, or the scattered marks across the white field—and what draws it away from that point?
ambiguities: The black rounded form could read as an animal, a head, or a purely abstract mass; no supplied metadata resolves this, so it is described by shape only.
nnxyz nnotb #157 shares the scattered-mark approach but its purple ground and face-like structure differ enough that a connection would rest mainly on title proximity, so it was not selected.
